topic: Finding once-a-year bills with a 20-minute email search and turning them into a monthly amount for your second number
pillar: The Three Numbers (what's coming in, what goes out, how many months you could keep going). Boring Money Monday.
caption:
Some bills only show up once a year, and they always seem to pick an awkward month.
Today, search your email for words like renewal, annual and registration.
Write each bill on one page with the amount and the month it arrives.
Add them up, divide by 12, and add that to your second number.
Save this so you can do it with your coffee next Monday.
The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is in my Stan store, link in bio.
Day one counts.

General education, not financial advice.

#boringmoneymonday #moneyafterdivorce #startingover #budgetingbasics #threenumbers

slides.title: The bills that only show up once a year
slides.subtitle: A 20-minute email search for Monday

slides.title: Your second number has quiet pieces
slides.body: Your second number is what goes out each month. A few bills only arrive once or twice a year, so they slip off the list. Today you go find them in your email.

slides.title: Search your inbox for these words
slides.body: Open your email on your phone or laptop. Try each word in the search bar.

slides.title: Write each one on a single page
slides.body: Keep it simple. One line per bill.
items: About how much it was last time
The month it usually shows up
A question mark if you are not sure

slides.title: Turn the list into a monthly amount
slides.body: Example with made-up numbers: car registration 120, home insurance 600. Together that's 720. Divide by 12 and you get 60 a month to add to your second number.

slides.title: Some bills need a second pair of eyes
slides.body: Property taxes or anything tied to your settlement can be tricky. A licensed professional can help with the details. For today, the list is enough.

slides.title: Keep this page with your numbers
slides.body: Save this for next Monday. The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet has a spot for these bills. It's in my Stan store, link in bio. Day one counts.
